content.text:
I submitted index 90 (Bi 0.11, Cu 0.52, V 0.37) as the best composition, but all three readings are tiny and may be no more than noise. I don't know whether it is actually good compared with the other 118 compositions.

I had only 3 photocurrent measurements for 121 candidates. The light is at 2.06 eV, which BiVO4 can't absorb (its band gap is about 2.4 eV) but copper vanadates can. So I aimed at the Cu-vanadate region with a little Bi added:

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 70 | 0.06 / 0.57 / 0.37 | about 0 |
| 90 | 0.11 / 0.52 / 0.37 | **4e-8** |
| 110 | 0.25 / 0.36 / 0.40 | −3e-8 |

- **What the data suggests:** a small amount of Bi seemed to help slightly, and more Bi with less Cu didn't.
- **What I didn't cover:** most of the library, including the Bi-rich compositions and the region around 0.18 Bi / 0.40 Cu / 0.42 V (indices 94, 96, 99).
- **XRD:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements before spending the photocurrent budget. They could have shown which crystal phases were present and helped choose where to measure.
